ev.maya-dental-jade.t: Maya nobles practise dental modification, and some lords wear jade set into their teeth.
ev.teotihuacan-decline.t: Teotihuacan, at its height from about AD 150 to 450, declines in the sixth century. Its sacking is recorded but not dated.
ev.turkic-khaganate-551.t: Bumin Khagan founds the first Turkic Khaganate on the Mongolian steppe in 551. It is destroyed by the Tang in 629–630.
ev.turks.t: Bumin broke the Rouran and founded the Göktürk khaganate in 551–552. The fall of the second khaganate in 744 set the Oghuz moving west; the Pechenegs reached the Pontic steppe in the late ninth century and the Cumans displaced the Kimeks in the eleventh. The Seljuks invaded Anatolia from the eleventh century, and the land became Turkish.
ev.muhammad-570.t: Muhammad is born at Mecca around 570.
ev.kongo-gumi-578.t: The builders Kongō Gumi are founded at Osaka in 578.
ev.sui-grand-canal.n: The Sui and the Grand Canal
ev.sui-grand-canal.t: The Sui reunite China in 581; the Grand Canal is completed in 604–609 to carry grain to the capital.
ev.gregory-590.t: Gregory the Great becomes pope in 590 and sends Augustine’s monks to England in 595.
ev.horyuji-607.t: The temple of Hōryū-ji at Ikaruga is believed completed in 607.
ev.heraclius-627.t: The Sasanians sack Jerusalem in 615 and take the True Cross; Khosrow II invades Egypt in 616. Heraclius defeats the Persians in 627, ending the Roman–Persian wars, five years before the Muslim conquests begin.
ev.pakal-615.t: K’inich Janaab’ Pakal becomes king of the Maya city of Palenque in 615.
ev.tang-founded.t: The Tang are founded on 18 June 618.
ev.hijra.t: Muhammad migrates from Mecca to Medina in 622, the year from which the Islamic calendar is counted.
ev.arab-conquests.t: Within eighty years of Muhammad's death in 632 Arab armies take Syria (Yarmouk 636), Persia (Qadisiyyah 636, Nahavand 642), Jerusalem (638), Egypt (642), Carthage (698), Spain (711), Sind and Transoxiana.
ev.qadisiyyah-636.t: The Muslim victory at al-Qadisiyyah in 636 opens Persia; Yazdegerd III is murdered at Merv in 651 and Sasanian rule ends. Palestine falls in 638 and Egypt in 639.
ev.dongola-652.t: The Arab armies are defeated in Nubia at Dongola in 642 and again in 652, and the baqt treaty follows.
ev.paper-money-650.t: China issues its first paper money in 650, under the Tang.
ev.umayyads-661.t: Ali is assassinated in 661 and Muawiyah I begins the Umayyad Caliphate at Damascus. Husayn is killed at Karbala in 680.
ev.silla-668.t: Tang and Silla defeat Baekje and its Yamato allies at Baekgang in 663; Goguryeo falls in 668 and Unified Silla rules the peninsula.
ev.carthage-698.t: Uqba ibn Nafi enters Ifriqiya in 670; the Arabs take Carthage from the Byzantines in 698.
ev.srivijaya-683.t: The pilgrim I-tsing visits Srivijaya in 671 on his way to Nalanda. From 683 Srivijaya holds the Straits of Malacca and Sunda, and in 686 it invades Java.
ev.greek-fire-677.t: The first Arab siege of Constantinople begins in 674; in 677 Greek fire destroys most of the Arab fleet.
ev.bulgaria-681.t: The Bulgars beat the Byzantines at Ongal in 680, and in 681 Byzantium recognises Bulgaria as independent.
ev.wu-zetian-690.t: Wu Zetian seizes power as Empress of China in 690 and makes Buddhism the state religion in 691.
ev.nara-710.t: Japan enacts the Taihō legal code in 701 and moves its capital to Heijō-kyō, Nara, in 710. The Nara period begins.
ev.al-andalus-711.t: Tariq ibn Ziyad crosses the strait at Gibraltar in 711 and al-Andalus is created; the Treaty of Tudmir follows in 713. In the same year, 711, Muhammad ibn al-Qasim invades Sindh.
ev.palenque-711.n: The wars of the Maya cities
ev.palenque-711.t: The Maya kingdoms of the Classic age fight among themselves: Toniná conquers Palenque in 711, and Quiriguá declares its independence from Copán in 738.
ev.constantinople-717.t: The Umayyad siege of Constantinople in 717–718 fails and the Arab advance into Europe from the east is halted. At Akroinon in 740 the Byzantines win their first large victory over the Arabs.
ev.iconoclasm-726.t: Leo III removes the image of Christ above the Chalke Gate in 726 and Iconoclasm begins. Empress Irene’s Seventh Ecumenical Council restores the icons in 787.
ev.bede-731.t: Bede completes the Ecclesiastical History of the English People in 731, a year before Tours.
ev.tours-732.t: Charles Martel halts the Umayyad advance at Tours in October 732.
ev.changan-742.t: A census of 742 counts 362,921 families and 1,960,188 people in the Chang’an district, the capital of Tang China under Xuanzong, whose reign of 712–756 is a high point for China.
ev.abbasids-750.t: The last Umayyad caliph, Marwan II, is overthrown and executed in 750, and the Abbasid Caliphate begins under al-Saffah. Al-Mansur succeeds him in 754; the Abbasids rule from Iraq.
ev.talas-751.t: An Abbasid army defeats a Tang force at Talas in 751, fixing Muslim rule over Transoxiana.
ev.paper-west-751.t: In the middle of the eighth century papermaking passes from China to the Arabs, in the years of the battle of Talas near Samarkand. The Han Chinese had made paper since the second century BC.
ev.an-lushan-755.t: The An Shi rebellion of 755–763 devastates Tang China, four years after the defeat at Talas.
ev.borobudur.t: Construction of Borobudur begins in Java around 760; the great Buddhist monument is completed under Samaratungga in 825.
ev.saxon-wars-772.t: Charlemagne campaigns against the Saxons for more than thirty years, from 772 to 804.
ev.lindisfarne-793.t: Vikings sack the monastery of Lindisfarne in 793, the first of the raids on Britain.
ev.norse-atlantic.t: The raid on Lindisfarne on 8 June 793 opened the Viking age. The Norse built the first longphorts in Ireland in 840, settled Iceland from about 870 and Greenland from 986, where the population may have reached about 5,000; the timber of L’Anse aux Meadows was felled in 1021. The Great Heathen Army landed in 865, the Danelaw was founded in 876 and Normandy was granted to Rollo in 911.
ev.heian-794.t: Emperor Kanmu moves the capital to Heian-kyō, today’s Kyoto, in 794.
ev.charlemagne-800.t: Pope Leo III crowns Charlemagne emperor at Rome on 25 December 800.
ev.maya-collapse.t: In the ninth century the political order of the central Maya lowlands collapses. The Post-Classic begins, and Chichén Itzá in the Yucatán becomes a regional capital.
ev.varangians.t: Swedish Vikings rowed the rivers of Russia to trade and settle: Rurik’s dynasty controlled Kiev and the road to the Black Sea, Constantinople took their goods and their swords, and Rus’ fleets raided the Caspian in 910, 912 and 943.
ev.khmer-802.t: Jayavarman II founds the Khmer empire in 802 and the Angkorian dynasty begins.
ev.leshan-803.t: The Giant Buddha carved in the rock at Leshan is completed in 803 after 90 years of work.
ev.algebra-820.t: Al-Khwarizmi writes his treatise on algebra at Baghdad around 820, and al-Ma’mun founds the House of Wisdom there in 830.
ev.verdun-843.t: The Treaty of Verdun divides the Carolingian Empire into three in 843, three years after the death of Louis the Pious.
ev.vikings-seville-844.t: Viking fleets raid Galicia and Asturias, then Lisbon and Seville, in 844.
ev.vikings-paris-845.t: A Viking fleet sails up the Seine and sacks Paris in 845.
ev.gunpowder-850.t: Chinese alchemists of the Tang invent gunpowder in the ninth century. Its first use in battle is recorded at Langshan Jiang in 919.
ev.igbo-ukwu.t: In the ninth century the Igbo of southern Nigeria cast elaborate bronzes, some of them buried with the dead at Igbo-Ukwu.
ev.karaouine-859.t: Al-Qarawiyyin is founded as a madrasa at Fez in 859.
ev.rurik-862.n: Rurik at Novgorod, Oleg at Kiev
ev.rurik-862.t: Rurik rules at Novgorod from 862 and Oleg takes Kiev in 882, the beginnings of Kievan Rus'.
ev.magyars.t: A joint attack by the Pechenegs and Bulgarians in 894 or 895 drove the Hungarians out of the Pontic steppe, their base at Etelköz; they crossed the north-eastern passes of the Carpathians in 895, took Transdanubia in 900, annihilated Moravia between 902 and 906 and destroyed an East Frankish army at Pressburg in 907.
ev.cyril-methodius-863.n: Cyril and Methodius among the Slavs
ev.cyril-methodius-863.t: Cyril and Methodius are sent to the Slavs in 863; their disciples reach Bulgaria in 885, where the Cyrillic script develops.
ev.bulgaria-864.t: Boris I of Bulgaria is baptised in 864.
ev.diamond-sutra-868.t: The Diamond Sutra, printed from woodblocks in 868, is the earliest known printed book.
ev.zanj-869.t: Enslaved East Africans rise against the Abbasids in southern Iraq in the Zanj rebellion of 869–883. In China the Huang Chao rebellion against the Tang follows in 875–884.
ev.alfred-878.t: Alfred the Great defeats Guthrum’s Danes at Ethandun in 878.
ev.fatimids-909.t: The Fatimid Caliphate rises among the Kutama of North Africa around 909. Cairo is founded beside Fustat in 969; it becomes the Fatimid capital in 972, and al-Azhar is established around 980.
ev.normandy-911.t: The treaty of Saint-Clair-sur-Epte gives Normandy to the Viking Rollo in 911.
ev.cordoba-929.t: Abd al-Rahman III takes the title of caliph at Córdoba in 929.
ev.goryeo-936.t: Goryeo unifies the Later Three Kingdoms of Korea in 936.
ev.bach-dang-938.t: Vietnamese forces win at the Bạch Đằng river in 938 and end the long Chinese domination of Vietnam.
ev.nri-948.t: The Nri kingdom of the Igbo begins in south-eastern Nigeria around 948.
ev.tui-tonga.t: The Tuʻi Tonga dynasty of Tonga is formed around 950. In the twelfth century its kings extend their reach across the islands of the western Pacific.
ev.lechfeld-955.t: Otto I defeats the Hungarians at the Lechfeld in 955; seven years later he is crowned emperor.
ev.otto-962.t: Otto I is crowned Holy Roman Emperor in 962.
ev.khazars-965.t: The prince of Kiev defeats the Khazar kingdom on the lower Volga in 965.
ev.ghaznavids-975.t: The Ghaznavids establish the first Turkic sultanate around 975 and conquer the Samanids in 999. The Seljuks convert to Islam in 960.
ev.gudit-980.t: Queen Gudit rises against the Aksumite dynasty of Abyssinia around 980.
ev.greenland-985.n: The Norse reach Greenland and America
ev.greenland-985.t: Erik the Red reaches Greenland in 985 and settlers follow in 986; timber at L'Anse aux Meadows in Newfoundland is dated to 1021.
ev.chichen-itza-987.t: In 987 Ah Mekat Tutul Xiu unites Uxmal, Mayapan and Chichén Itzá in the Yucatán, which becomes a regional capital of the Post-Classic Maya.
ev.kiev-988.t: Vladimir of Kiev has the idols thrown down and the people baptised in the Dnieper in 988.
ev.tiwanaku-collapse.t: The Tiwanaku state by Lake Titicaca collapses in the first half of the eleventh century. In Mexico the Toltec and Mixtec civilisations flourish.
ev.thule.t: The Thule culture formed on the Alaskan coast by AD 1000 and spread east across the Canadian Arctic with dog sleds, umiaks and whaling, reaching Greenland by the thirteenth century; the Dorset were gone by about 1300. They met the Norse, who called them Skrælingjar.
ev.ghazni-1001.t: Mahmud of Ghazni begins his raids into northern India in 1001.
ev.ibn-al-haytham-1011.t: Held under house arrest in Cairo from 1011 to 1021, Ibn al-Haytham writes his Book of Optics. Cairo’s Dar al-Hikma had been founded in 1004.
ev.kleidion-1014.t: Basil II defeats Samuil of Bulgaria at Kleidion in 1014 and by 1018 has conquered the First Bulgarian Empire. In Ireland Brian Boru is killed winning at Clontarf in 1014.
ev.chola-srivijaya-1025.t: Rajendra Chola I’s navy strikes across the Bay of Bengal in 1025 and makes Srivijaya a vassal. He moves his capital to Gangaikonda Cholapuram.
ev.jordan-quake-1033.t: An earthquake and tsunami strike the Jordan valley and the coast of Palestine in 1033 and kill tens of thousands.
ev.bi-sheng-1041.t: In the years 1041–1048 Bi Sheng makes ceramic movable type in Song China, four centuries before Gutenberg. The Song military manual Wujing Zongyao of 1044 gives formulas for gunpowder.
ev.cahokia.t: The Mississippian culture flourishes in the eleventh century. Its great town at Cahokia, on the Mississippi below the Missouri, grows in the thirteenth century to a population that rivals London’s.
ev.schism-1054.t: Rome and Constantinople excommunicate each other in 1054; the churches of East and West divide.
ev.crab-supernova-1054.t: Chinese astronomers record a new star in 1054, the year of the Great Schism. Its remnant is the Crab Nebula.
ev.seljuks-baghdad-1055.t: The Seljuk Turks take Baghdad in 1055, beat the Byzantines at Manzikert in 1071 and take Jerusalem from the Fatimids in 1074. Pope Urban II calls the First Crusade in 1095.
ev.anawrahta-1057.t: Anawrahta of Pagan defeats Thaton in 1057 and unifies Myanmar.
ev.banu-hilal-1057.t: Arab tribes of the Banu Hilal invade Ifriqiya and destroy Kairouan in 1057.
ev.norman-conquest.t: William crosses from Normandy and wins at Hastings in 1066, the year Harold had beaten the Norwegians at Stamford Bridge.
ev.manzikert-1071.t: The Seljuks under Alp Arslan defeat the Byzantines in Anatolia in 1071.
ev.koumbi-1076.t: The Almoravids sack Koumbi Saleh, capital of the Ghana Empire, in 1076. Ten years later they cross to Spain and defeat Castile at az-Zallaqah, a year after Alfonso VI took Toledo.
ev.canossa-1077.t: Emperor Henry IV humbles himself before Pope Gregory VII at Canossa in 1077.
ev.bologna-1088.t: The University of Bologna is established in 1088.
ev.compass-1088.t: Shen Kuo’s Dream Pool Essays of 1088 first describe the magnetic needle compass. Su Song’s astronomical clock tower at Kaifeng is finished in 1094.
ev.first-crusade.t: Urban II calls the crusade at Clermont in 1095; the armies gather at Constantinople, take Nicaea and Antioch and storm Jerusalem in 1099.
ev.ife-1200.t: The Ife Empire of the Yoruba is established in West Africa in the twelfth century; it collapses around 1420.
ev.mayapan.t: Mayapan rises to dominance in the Yucatán in the twelfth century after the decline of Chichén Itzá, whose Great Ballcourt is the largest in Mesoamerica; it is abandoned around 1448.
ev.venice-arsenal-1104.t: Venice founds its Arsenal in 1104, the shipyard that in time employs about 16,000 workers.
ev.angkor-wat-1113.t: Suryavarman II is crowned at Angkor in 1113, and under him Angkor Wat is built.
ev.templars-1119.t: The Knights Templar are founded at Jerusalem in 1119; the Teutonic Knights follow at Acre in 1198.
ev.didgori-1121.t: The Georgians, 45,000 strong with their allies, defeat a Seljuk-led coalition at Didgori in 1121. Tbilisi becomes the Georgian capital in 1122, ending 400 years of Arab rule.
ev.jin-song-1127.t: The Jurchen Jin declare war on the Song in 1125 and take northern China in 1127. The Southern Song found China’s first permanent standing navy in 1132; by 1183 it has 52,000 men, and the treaty of 1141 sets the border on the Huai.
ev.chaco-collapse.t: A fifty-year drought settles on the American Southwest from 1130, and the Chaco Canyon culture of the Ancestral Puebloans collapses between 1140 and 1150.
ev.st-denis-1136.t: Abbot Suger begins rebuilding the abbey church of Saint-Denis north of Paris in 1136, and the Gothic style begins.
ev.almohads-1147.n: The Almohads and the siege of Lisbon
ev.almohads-1147.t: The Almohads take North Africa from the Almoravids in 1147; the same year crusaders and Portuguese take Lisbon after a four-month siege.
ev.tula-toltec.t: Tula, the city of the Toltecs, burns in the twelfth century and the Toltec empire ends.
ev.idrisi-1154.t: Al-Idrisi publishes his Geography in 1154, the year Henry II is crowned in England.
ev.saladin-1171.t: Saladin ends the Fatimid Caliphate in Egypt in 1171 and founds the Ayyubid dynasty. Sixteen years later he destroys the crusader army at Hattin.
ev.genpei-1180.t: The Minamoto and the Taira fight the Genpei War in Japan from 1180 to 1185. Hōnen had founded the Pure Land sect in 1175.
ev.windmills-1185.t: The first record of windmills in Europe dates from 1185.
ev.hattin-1187.t: Saladin destroys the army of the Kingdom of Jerusalem at the Horns of Hattin on 4 July 1187 and takes Jerusalem. The Third Crusade follows; Barbarossa drowns in the Salef in 1190.
ev.ghori-1192.t: Muhammad of Ghor establishes the first Muslim empire in northern India in 1192; the monastery-university of Nalanda is destroyed in 1193.
ev.fourth-crusade-1204.t: The crusaders sack Zadar for Venice in 1202 and Constantinople in 1204.
ev.fibonacci-1202.t: Fibonacci introduces the Liber Abaci in 1202.
ev.genghis-1206.t: Temüjin is elected khan of all the Mongols in 1206 and takes the name Genghis Khan.
ev.delhi-sultanate-1206.t: The Delhi Sultanate is established in northern India in 1206 under the Mamluk dynasty, the year Genghis Khan is proclaimed.
ev.mongols.t: Temüjin was proclaimed Genghis Khan in 1206; Zhongdu fell in 1215, Bukhara and Samarkand in 1220, Ryazan in December 1237 and Kiev on 6 December 1240. Legnica and Mohi were fought two days apart in April 1241, Baghdad was sacked in 1258 and the advance was stopped at Ain Jalut in 1260. Up to half of Hungary’s roughly two million people died in the invasion.
ev.mongol-conquests.t: From Genghis Khan's invasion of the Jin in 1211 to Kublai's victory at Yamen in 1279 the Mongols take north China, Khwarazm (Otrar and Samarkand in 1220), the Rus' lands (1237–1240), Baghdad (1258) and the Song.
ev.las-navas-1212.n: The Battle of Las Navas de Tolosa
ev.las-navas-1212.t: The Christian kingdoms defeat the Almohads at Las Navas de Tolosa in 1212. Portugal completes its reconquest with the Algarve in 1249.
ev.magna-carta.t: King John seals Magna Carta at Runnymede on 15 June 1215.
ev.mapungubwe-1220.t: The kingdom of Mapungubwe is established on the Limpopo around 1220. Later in the century the Kingdom of Zimbabwe is founded, and in Ethiopia the Solomonic dynasty replaces the Zagwe in 1270.
ev.khwarazm-1221.t: The Mongols destroy Merv, Herat, Bamyan and Nishapur in 1221, the cities of the Khwarazmian Empire.
ev.kalka-1223.t: A Mongol army defeats the Russian princes on the Kalka river in 1223, fourteen years before the great invasion.
ev.mali-empire-1235.t: The Mandinka kingdoms unite to form the Mali Empire in 1235.
ev.mongols-rus-1237.n: The Mongol invasion of Rus and Europe
ev.mongols-rus-1237.t: The Mongols conquer Kievan Rus in 1237–1240. In 1241 they defeat the Poles at Legnica and the Hungarians at Mohi.
ev.neva-peipus-1240.t: Russians defeat a Swedish army on the Neva in 1240 and the Teutonic Knights on the ice of Lake Peipus in 1242.
ev.mesa-verde-1250.t: Cliff Palace and the other Ancestral Pueblo towns of Mesa Verde reach their height around 1250.
ev.polynesians-aotearoa.t: The last great landmass to be settled: radiocarbon dates from over 500 sites place the first Māori settlement of the North Island between AD 1250 and 1275, and the main settlement perhaps between 1320 and 1350 as a coordinated migration in large waka. Within two centuries the moa were gone.
ev.baghdad-1258.t: The Mongols take and destroy Baghdad in 1258 and end the Abbasid Caliphate.
ev.ain-jalut-1260.t: The Mamluks of Egypt inflict the first major defeat on the Mongols at Ain Jalut in 1260. The Mamluks take Antioch in 1268 and Acre, the last crusader city, in 1291.
ev.aquinas-1265.t: Thomas Aquinas begins the Summa Theologiae in 1265. In 1277 the bishop of Paris condemns propositions drawn from Aristotle.
ev.marco-polo.n: Marco Polo’s journey to Kublai Khan
ev.marco-polo.t: Niccolò, Maffeo and the young Marco Polo leave Venice in 1271, sail to Acre and Hormuz and ride the Silk Road to Kublai Khan’s summer palace at Shangdu, probably in 1275. Marco serves the Khan for seventeen years. They sail home in 1291 escorting the princess Kököchin; only 18 of about 600 passengers survive, and the Polos reach Venice in 1295, where Marco later dictates his book to Rustichello da Pisa in a Genoese prison.
ev.mongol-japan-1274.t: Kublai Khan’s fleets invade Japan in 1274 and 1281 and are both times repelled.
ev.song-ends-1279.t: The Song dynasty ends with defeat by the Mongols at sea off Yamen in 1279, and all China is under Yuan rule.
ev.majapahit-1293.t: A Mongol invasion of Java is repelled in 1293 and Majapahit is founded in eastern Java the same year.
ev.wooden-type-1298.t: Wang Zhen invents wooden movable type in China in 1298.
ev.ottomans-1299.t: Osman I establishes the Ottoman state in north-western Anatolia in 1299.
ev.avignon-1309.t: The papal seat moves from Rome to Avignon in 1309 and stays until 1377. The return is followed in 1378 by the Western Schism, with two and then three rival popes until 1417.
ev.great-famine-1315.t: Years of rain and failed harvests from 1315 to 1317 bring the Great Famine to northern Europe. Millions die, a generation before the Black Death.
ev.divine-comedy-1321.t: Dante completes the Divine Comedy in 1321, the poem of a journey through Hell, Purgatory and Paradise.
ev.mansa-musa-1324.t: In the seventeenth year of his reign Musa I of Mali goes on pilgrimage to Mecca with about 60,000 men and 80 camels each carrying 300 pounds of gold. He floods the Cairo market with so much gold that its value had not recovered twelve years later; on the way home he brings the poet and architect al-Sahili, who builds him a mosque at Timbuktu.
ev.ibn-battuta.t: Ibn Battuta leaves Tangier for Mecca on 14 June 1325 and travels for almost thirty years: Cairo, Baghdad, the Swahili coast, the Golden Horde and Constantinople, Delhi, where he serves Muhammad bin Tughluq as a judge, the Maldives and Quanzhou. He crosses the Sahara to Mali and Timbuktu in 1352 and dictates the Rihla to Ibn Juzayy around 1355.
ev.tenochtitlan-1325.t: The Mexica found Tenochtitlan on an island in Lake Texcoco in 1325. Acamapichtli is accepted as its first tlatoani in 1366; within a century the island town is the capital of the Aztec Empire.
ev.vijayanagara-1336.t: Harihara I founds the Vijayanagara Empire in South India in 1336. It rules the south for more than two centuries, until the Deccan sultanates defeat it at Talikota in 1565.
ev.hundred-years-war.t: War between England and France begins in 1337.
ev.black-death.t: Graves near Issyk-Kul dated 1338–39 carry plague inscriptions, and Yersinia pestis DNA has been found in teeth there. Jani Beg’s Golden Horde army, itself sick, besieged the Genoese port of Kaffa in 1346; the disease reached Constantinople in the summer of 1347 and Sicily with twelve Genoese galleys in October. Genoa, Venice and Marseille had it in January 1348, France, Iberia and England by June, Norway in 1349, northern Russia in 1352 and Moscow in 1353.
ev.ayutthaya-1350.t: Ramathibodi I establishes the kingdom of Ayutthaya in Siam in 1350; Fa Ngum founds Lan Xang in Laos three years later.
ev.hansa-1356.t: The first Diet of the Hansa meets at Lübeck in 1356 and formalises the Hanseatic League, the merchant league of the Baltic and North Sea towns.
ev.ming-1368.t: The Red Turban rebellions, begun along the Huai in 1351, end Mongol Yuan rule. The Yuan dynasty ends and the Ming dynasty begins in 1368, with its first capital at Nanjing.
ev.timur.t: Timur founds his dynasty at Samarkand in 1370 and captures the Ottoman sultan Bayezid at Ankara in 1402.
ev.kulikovo-1380.t: A Muscovite force defeats the Horde at Kulikovo Field in 1380.
ev.peasants-revolt-1381.t: English peasants rise in 1381, the year Wycliffe is dismissed from Oxford. It is the century of revolts after the plague: the Ciompi in Florence (1378–82) and the Red Turbans in China.
ev.tokhtamysh-1382.t: Two years after Kulikovo, Khan Tokhtamysh of the Golden Horde takes Moscow in 1382. The Horde’s overlordship of the Russian principalities lasts another century.
ev.kosovo-1389.t: The Ottomans and the Serbs meet at Kosovo Polje in 1389; Prince Lazar and Sultan Murad I are both killed. At Nicopolis on the Danube in 1396 the Ottomans defeat a large crusader army, and the Second Bulgarian Empire ends with Vidin the same year.
ev.joseon-1392.t: Taejo founds the Joseon dynasty in Korea in 1392, the same year Japan’s two rival courts are reunited.
ev.kalmar-1397.t: Norway, Sweden and Denmark are united under one crown at Kalmar in 1397.
ev.ankara-1402.t: Timur defeats the Ottomans at Ankara in 1402 and captures Sultan Bayezid I. Ten years of civil war among Bayezid’s sons follow, the Ottoman Interregnum of 1403–1413.
ev.malacca-1402.t: Parameswara, a prince who fled Palembang, founds Malacca on the strait in 1402. It becomes the great port between the Indian Ocean and the China Sea until Albuquerque takes it in 1511.
ev.zheng-he.t: Seven fleets sail from Nanjing between 1405 and 1433 to Champa, Java, Malacca, Ceylon and Calicut and, from the fourth voyage, to Hormuz, Aden and the African coast as far as Malindi; the voyages end in 1433, the year Zheng He dies.
ev.grunwald-1410.t: Poland and Lithuania defeat the Teutonic Knights at Grunwald in 1410, the beginning of the order’s downfall.
ev.agincourt-1415.t: Henry V defeats the French at Agincourt in 1415.
ev.ceuta-1415.t: Henry the Navigator takes Ceuta in 1415, the first Portuguese foothold in Africa and the start of a century of voyages down the African coast.
ev.jan-hus-1415.t: The Council of Constance burns the Bohemian reformer Jan Hus in 1415. The Hussite Wars follow in Bohemia from 1419 and end at Lipany in 1434.
ev.forbidden-city-1420.t: The Yongle Emperor moves the Ming capital to Beijing, and the Forbidden City is completed in 1420.
ev.itzcoatl-1427.t: Itzcoatl begins his reign at Tenochtitlan in 1427 and is counted the first Aztec emperor; Moctezuma I follows in 1440. The city on the lake becomes the head of an empire of tribute.
ev.orleans-1429.t: Joan of Arc ends the English siege of Orléans in 1429. She is tried at Rouen and burned there on 30 May 1431, aged nineteen.
ev.coca-andes.t: The Inca hold the coca leaf sacred and use it in moderation against hunger and pain; the chasqui runners who carry messages on the roads chew it for strength.
ev.inca-expansion.t: Pachacuti begins the expansion of the Inca state from Cusco in 1438. Topa Inca conquers the Chimú kingdom from 1463 and pushes north into Ecuador; in the south the empire reaches the Maule in Chile. By about 1527 Tawantinsuyu covers some 2,000,000 km², with about 12 million people, linked by roads, runners and knotted quipu records; Pizarro takes Atahualpa at Cajamarca in 1532.
ev.gutenberg-press.t: Gutenberg's press with movable type at Mainz is dated 1439 by the timeline.
ev.benin-ewuare-1440.t: Oba Ewuare comes to power in Benin around 1440 and builds up the kingdom and its city in West Africa.
ev.atlantic-captives-1441.t: In 1441 a Portuguese ship brings captives from West Africa directly to Portugal. It is the start of the Portuguese seaborne trade in enslaved Africans.
ev.hangul-1443.t: King Sejong of Joseon publishes hangul in 1443, an alphabet made for Korean. King Taejong’s court had first used movable type in 1403.
ev.tumu-1449.t: The Oirat leader Esen captures the Zhengtong Emperor at Tumu Fortress in 1449.
ev.huanchaco-1450.t: On a bluff near Huanchaco, on the Chimú coast of Peru, more than 140 children aged about 5 to 14 and some 200 young llamas are sacrificed around 1450. The excavators, Gabriel Prieto and John Verano, think it was an offering against El Niño rains and floods; their 2019 paper in PLOS ONE counts 137 children.
ev.machu-picchu.t: The Inca build Machu Picchu on a ridge above the Urubamba in the 1450s, in the years of Pachacuti’s expansion.
ev.constantinople-1453.t: Constantinople falls to the Ottomans in 1453.
ev.gutenberg-bible-1455.t: Johann Gutenberg’s shop at Mainz prints a large-format Latin Bible between 1454 and 1456, the first great book of European printing. More than 150 copies are made; about 20 survive complete. Gutenberg may have begun working on the technique as early as the 1430s.
ev.onin-1467.t: Civil war breaks out in 1467 and opens the Sengoku period, more than a century of warring states in Japan.
ev.novgorod-1478.t: Muscovy annexes the merchant republic of Novgorod in 1478. Two years later the stand on the Ugra ends the Horde’s overlordship.
ev.ugra-1480.t: Ivan III's forces deter Akhmat Khan on the Ugra in 1480; Moscow pays tribute no more.
ev.dias-1488.t: Bartolomeu Dias sails round the southern tip of Africa in 1488 and proves the sea route east. Six years earlier Diogo Cão had entered the mouth of the Congo.
ev.granada-1492.t: Granada, the last Muslim kingdom in Iberia, falls in 1492.
ev.columbus-1492.t: Columbus leaves Palos on 3 August 1492, makes landfall at Guanahani on 12 October and reports to the monarchs in Barcelona in March 1493.
ev.alhambra-decree-1492.n: The expulsion of the Jews from Spain
ev.alhambra-decree-1492.t: The Alhambra Decree of 1492 orders the Jews of Spain to convert or leave. Between 40,000 and 200,000 leave, the year Granada falls and Columbus sails.
ev.tordesillas-1494.t: Spain and Portugal divide the newly found lands along a line west of Cape Verde in 1494.
ev.da-gama.t: Vasco da Gama leaves Lisbon in July 1497, rounds the Cape, crosses the Indian Ocean and reaches Calicut on 20 May 1498; he is home in 1499, two years and two days after sailing.
ev.brazil-1500.t: Cabral's fleet sights Monte Pascoal and lands at Porto Seguro in April 1500.
ev.guru-nanak-1500.n: Guru Nanak and the Sikh faith
ev.guru-nanak-1500.t: Guru Nanak, born in the Punjab in 1469, begins to preach around 1500. His teaching is the beginning of Sikhism.
ev.safavid-1501.t: The Safavid dynasty reunifies Iran in 1501 and rules until 1736. Ottomans and Safavids fight at Chaldiran in 1514, and the Ottomans take Baghdad from them in 1534.
ev.kongo-afonso-1506.t: Afonso I wins the battle of Mbanza Kongo in 1506 and makes Catholicism the state religion of the kingdom of Kongo.
ev.albuquerque-1507.t: Afonso de Albuquerque takes Hormuz and Muscat in 1507, Goa in 1510 and Malacca in 1511. The victory at Diu in 1509 begins Portuguese dominance of the spice trade.
ev.smallpox-hispaniola-1507.t: The first recorded smallpox epidemic in the New World devastates the Taíno of Hispaniola in 1507. Five years earlier the first enslaved Africans had been reported in the Americas.
ev.sistine-ceiling-1508.t: Michelangelo paints the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel from 1508 to 1512, a few years after his David for Florence and his Pietà for Rome.
ev.prince-1513.t: Machiavelli writes The Prince in 1513, the year Balboa crosses the isthmus of Panama and sees the Pacific.
ev.atlantic-slave-trade.t: Twelve and a half million captives departed Africa for the Americas between 1514 and 1866, and 10.7 million disembarked; the Trans-Atlantic database documents more than 36,000 voyages, about two-thirds of all that sailed. The largest forced migration in history, it peopled Brazil and the Caribbean and the plantations of the American South.
ev.ottoman-egypt-1517.t: Selim I defeats the Mamluks in 1516–1517 and gains Egypt, Arabia and the Levant. Under Suleiman from 1520 the empire reaches its zenith: Belgrade in 1521, Rhodes in 1522, Mohács in 1526.
ev.reformation-1517.t: Luther posts the Ninety-five Theses at Wittenberg in 1517; the Reformation begins.
ev.smallpox-americas.t: Smallpox had ravaged Hispaniola for two years when Pánfilo de Narváez landed at Veracruz on 23 April 1520 and carried it into Mexico. It killed most of the Aztec army and about a quarter of the people before Cortés took Tenochtitlan in 1521. When it reached the Inca empire it killed the emperor Huayna Capac, his successor and most of the other leaders within months.
ev.cortes.t: Cortés lands near Veracruz in April 1519, allies with Tlaxcala, enters Tenochtitlan on 8 November, is driven out on the Noche Triste in 1520 and takes the city on 13 August 1521 after a siege.
ev.magellan.t: Magellan's fleet leaves Seville on 10 August 1519 and passes the strait on 28 November 1520; Magellan is killed at Mactan in 1521 and Elcano brings the Victoria home on 6 September 1522.
ev.peasants-war-1524.t: Peasants rise across the Holy Roman Empire in 1524–1525, seven years after Luther’s theses.
ev.mohacs-1526.t: Suleiman defeats and kills Louis II of Hungary at Mohács in 1526.
ev.panipat-1526.t: On 21 April 1526 Babur, with about 12,000 men, matchlocks and cannon, defeats Ibrahim Lodi’s 50,000 or more and 1,000 war elephants at Panipat. Ibrahim and about 20,000 of his men are killed; the guns panic the elephants, and the victory founds the Mughal Empire.
ev.sack-rome-1527.t: Troops of Charles V sack Rome in 1527, two years after his armies captured Francis I of France at Pavia.
ev.vienna-1529.t: Suleiman's army reaches Vienna on 27 September 1529 and abandons the siege on 14 October.
ev.church-england-1532.t: The Church of England breaks from Rome in 1531–1532 under Henry VIII; Anne Boleyn is beheaded in 1536.
ev.peru-1532.t: The Spanish conquest of the Inca empire begins in 1532 and the Inca capital is in Spanish hands within a year.
ev.sao-vicente-1532.n: São Vicente, the first Portuguese town in Brazil
ev.sao-vicente-1532.t: São Vicente, founded in 1532, is the first permanent Portuguese settlement in the Americas. Buenos Aires is founded by Pedro de Mendoza in 1536 and Cartier claims Canada for France in 1534.
ev.copernicus-1543.t: Copernicus's heliocentric treatise appears in 1543, the year he dies at Frombork.
ev.nanban-1543.t: Portuguese traders reach Japan in 1543 and open the Nanban trade. Firearms are used on a Japanese battlefield at Uedahara in 1548.
ev.trent.t: The council that shapes the Catholic Counter-Reformation sits at Trent from 1545 to 1563.
ev.cocoliztli-1545.t: The disease seems to have emerged in the highlands near modern Puebla in 1545 and ravaged the Valley of Mexico, where many Indigenous towns were abandoned. It may have reached Sinaloa, Chiapas and Guatemala, but kept to high ground and nearly spared the coasts. The cemetery of Teposcolula-Yucundaa in Oaxaca is the only one conclusively tied to it.
ev.kazan-1552.t: Kazan falls to Ivan IV after a siege in 1552 and Astrakhan is annexed in 1556; the Volga is Russian to the Caspian.
ev.shaanxi-1556.t: The Shaanxi earthquake of 1556 is the deadliest known in the Ming era. The same year Akbar wins the second battle of Panipat.
ev.spain-bankrupt-1557.t: Habsburg Spain declares bankruptcy in 1557, the first of four state bankruptcies under Philip II (1557, 1560, 1575, 1596).
ev.manila-galleon.t: From 1565 galleons link Manila and Acapulco, once Urdaneta finds the eastward route.
ev.talikota-1565.t: The Deccan sultanates defeat the Vijayanagara Empire at Talikota in 1565.
ev.lepanto-1571.t: The Holy League's galleys defeat the Ottoman fleet at Lepanto in 1571.
ev.st-bartholomew-1572.t: Huguenots are massacred in Paris on St Bartholomew’s Day 1572. The French Wars of Religion end only with the Edict of Nantes in 1598.
ev.alcazarquivir-1578.t: King Sebastian of Portugal is killed fighting in Morocco in 1578. In 1580 Spain and Portugal are united under Philip II, for sixty years.
ev.gregorian-1582.t: The Gregorian calendar is introduced in 1582 and ten days are skipped to bring the year back into line with the sun.
ev.japan-unified-1590.t: After Oda Nobunaga’s death at Honnō-ji in 1582, Toyotomi Hideyoshi completes the unification of Japan with the siege of Odawara in 1590.
ev.armada-1588.t: Philip II’s Armada leaves Lisbon on 30 May 1588 with 138 ships and over 25,000 seamen and soldiers to carry an army from Flanders to England. It is sighted off the Lizard on 29 July and fought up the Channel; eight English fireships break its anchorage off Calais on the night of 7 August and the fleet is beaten at Gravelines on 8 August. Driven north round Scotland and Ireland, about 19 ships are wrecked; only around 67 return to Spain and up to 11,000 men may have died.
ev.tondibi-1591.t: A Moroccan army defeats the Songhai Empire at Tondibi in 1591; the old Mali Empire is defeated at Jenné in 1599.
ev.imjin-1592.t: Hideyoshi’s armies invade Korea twice between 1592 and 1598. Korea, with Ming help, repels both invasions; the war ends with Hideyoshi’s death in 1598.
ev.dutch-indies-1595.n: The first Dutch voyage to the Indies
ev.dutch-indies-1595.t: The first Dutch expedition sails for the East Indies in 1595 with 249 men and 64 cannon. Seven years later the Dutch East India Company is founded.
ev.romeo-juliet-1597.t: Romeo and Juliet is published in 1597. Shakespeare, baptised in 1564, is the same age as Galileo, born at Pisa that February.
ev.bruno-1600.t: Giordano Bruno is burned for heresy in Rome in 1600.
ev.eic-charter-1600.n: The East India Company is chartered
ev.eic-charter-1600.t: On 31 December 1600 Elizabeth I grants a royal charter to the Earl of Cumberland and 218 others trading to the East Indies. James Lancaster sails on the first voyage in the Red Dragon in 1601; the Company opens trading posts at Surat and Madras and moves to Calcutta after 1690.
ev.sekigahara-1600.t: Tokugawa Ieyasu wins the battle of Sekigahara in 1600, two years after Hideyoshi’s death. In 1603 he becomes shogun and the Edo period begins; it lasts until 1868.
ev.time-of-troubles.n: The Time of Troubles and the Romanovs
ev.time-of-troubles.t: Famine in 1601–1603 kills about a third of Russia’s people. A Polish–Lithuanian army beats the Russians and Swedes at Klushino in 1610 and takes Moscow; in 1613 the Time of Troubles ends with the election of the first Romanov tsar, whose dynasty rules until 1917.
ev.voc-1602.t: The Dutch trading companies merge into the VOC in 1602.
ev.ricci-map-1602.n: Matteo Ricci’s map of the world
ev.ricci-map-1602.t: The Jesuit Matteo Ricci makes a map of the world in China in 1602; it is used across East Asia.
ev.tokugawa-1603.t: Tokugawa Ieyasu takes the title of shogun in 1603 and rules from Edo.
ev.janszoon-1606.t: Willem Janszoon makes the first recorded European landing on the Australian mainland in 1606.
ev.jamestown-1607.t: The English settle Jamestown in Virginia in 1607.
ev.galileo-1610.t: Galileo observes the moons of Jupiter in 1610.
ev.thirty-years-war.t: Thirty years of war across the Empire, from Prague in 1618 to the Peace of Westphalia in 1648; the French beat Spain's tercios at Rocroi in 1643.
ev.batavia-1619.t: The Dutch hold Jayakarta against a siege in 1619 and build Batavia on its site, the capital of the VOC’s Asian empire. Sultan Agung of Mataram fails to take it in 1628–1629.
ev.first-africans-virginia-1619.t: The first Africans are brought to Virginia in 1619, twelve years after Jamestown. In 1622 Algonquian warriors kill 347 settlers outside Jamestown.
ev.mayflower-1620.t: The Mayflower sails from Plymouth to New England in 1620.
ev.taj-mahal-1632.t: Shah Jahan begins the Taj Mahal at Agra in 1632. His son Aurangzeb deposes him in 1658.
ev.galileo-trial-1633.t: Galileo stands trial before the Inquisition in Rome in 1633.
ev.sakoku-1639.t: After the Shimabara rebellion of Christians and peasants in 1637, Japan becomes a locked country under sakoku between 1633 and 1639.
ev.scientific-instruments-1642.t: Blaise Pascal builds a mechanical calculator in 1642 and Evangelista Torricelli the mercury barometer in 1643. Huygens makes the first working pendulum clock in 1657.
ev.qing-1644.t: The Manchu conquest ends the Ming in 1644; the Qing rule from Beijing.
ev.westphalia-1648.t: The peace of 1648 ends the Thirty Years' War and the Eighty Years' War.
ev.khmelnytsky-1648.t: Bohdan Khmelnytsky’s Cossacks rise against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth in 1648, the year of the Peace of Westphalia.
ev.charles-i-1649.t: Charles I is executed for high treason in 1649, after the civil war that began in 1642.
ev.royal-society-1660.t: The Royal Society is founded in London in 1660. Robert Hooke sees cells through a microscope in 1665 and Antonie van Leeuwenhoek discovers bacteria in 1676.
ev.mbwila-1665.t: Portugal defeats the kingdom of Kongo at Mbwila in Angola in 1665.
ev.great-plague-london.t: Plague probably came from the Netherlands, where Amsterdam suffered in 1663–64, and the first deaths were in the docks and the parish of St Giles. A merchant’s cloth from London carried it to Eyam in Derbyshire, which shut itself in and lost about a third of its people. The epidemic had largely subsided before the Great Fire of September 1666.
ev.great-fire-london-1666.t: The Great Fire of London burns the old city in 1666.
ev.shivaji-1674.t: Shivaji crowns himself Chhatrapati in 1674 and founds the Maratha Empire against the Mughals. He had visited Aurangzeb at Agra in 1666.
ev.pueblo-revolt-1680.t: The Pueblo peoples rise in 1680 and drive the Spanish out of New Mexico until 1692.
ev.la-salle-1682.t: Robert de La Salle claims the lands of the Mississippi for France in 1682. New Orleans is founded in 1718.
ev.vienna-1683.t: The Ottoman army besieges Vienna in 1683; the Holy League relieves the city, and the Great Turkish War ends at Karlowitz in 1699 with Hungary ceded to the Habsburgs.
ev.taiwan-1683.t: The Qing conquer the Kingdom of Tungning in 1683 and annex Taiwan, the year the Ottomans fail before Vienna.
ev.glorious-revolution.t: William of Orange lands in England in 1688; the settlement of 1689 makes England a constitutional monarchy.
ev.bank-of-england-1694.t: The Bank of England is established in 1694, in the reign of William and Mary after the Glorious Revolution.
ev.azov-1696.t: Peter’s first siege of Azov in 1695 fails. In 1696 he returns with about 75,000 men and a fleet built at Voronezh of two ships of the line, four fireships and 23 galleys; the Ottoman garrison of about 7,000 surrenders on 19 July. The Boyar Duma’s decree of 20 October 1696 is counted the birth of the Russian navy, and Taganrog becomes its first base.
ev.grand-embassy.t: The Grand Embassy sets out on 9 March 1697 with the tsar travelling incognito as Peter Mikhailov. He is refused a look at the fortifications of Riga, spends two months with an artillery engineer at Königsberg, reaches Zaandam on 18 August 1697 and works in the Amsterdam yards, then lives at Deptford from January to April 1698. News of the Streltsy rising cuts short his stay in Vienna and he is back in Moscow in early September 1698.
ev.nojpeten-1697.t: Martín de Ursúa takes the Itza capital Nojpetén in 1697, and independent Maya rule ends, 176 years after the fall of Tenochtitlan.
ev.karlowitz-1699.t: The Treaty of Karlowitz in 1699 cedes most of Hungary to the Habsburgs. The Ottoman retreat from central Europe has begun.
ev.ashanti-1701.t: The battle of Feyiase in 1701 marks the rise of the Asante Empire in the forest of the Gold Coast.
ev.st-petersburg-1703.t: Peter founds Saint Petersburg on Hare Island in the Neva on 29 June 1703.
ev.aurangzeb-1707.t: Aurangzeb dies in 1707 and the Mughal Empire begins to break apart; in the same year the Act of Union joins the parliaments of Scotland and England.
ev.poltava-1709.t: Peter's army defeats Charles XII of Sweden at Poltava on 27 June 1709.
ev.newcomen-1712.t: Thomas Newcomen’s steam engine of 1712 pumps water from mines, thirteen years after Thomas Savery showed a steam pump to the Royal Society. Cristofori had built the first piano in Florence in 1709.
ev.south-sea-bubble-1720.t: Shares in the South Sea Company soar and collapse in London in 1720, the year the Great Plague of Marseille begins.
ev.great-plague-marseille.t: The merchant ship Grand-Saint-Antoine left Sidon, called at Smyrna, Tripoli and plague-struck Cyprus, was refused at Livorno and reached Marseille in May 1720; merchants pressed to land its silk and cotton from quarantine. Plague broke out in the city within days and spread to Aix, Arles, Apt and Toulon. The Parlement of Aix made contact with Marseille a capital offence, and a dry-stone plague wall was raised across the country to enforce it.
ev.nystad-1721.t: The treaty of 1721 ends the Great Northern War; Russia gains Ingria, Estonia and Livonia and Peter is proclaimed emperor.
ev.lomonosov-1730.t: In 1730 Mikhail Lomonosov, a nineteen-year-old from the village of Mishaninskaya near Kholmogory on the White Sea, walks all the way to Moscow to study. He enters the Slavic Greek Latin Academy by claiming to be a nobleman’s son; in 1755 he helps Count Shuvalov found Moscow University.
ev.delhi-1739.t: Nader Shah of Persia invades and plunders Delhi in 1739.
ev.bering-1741.t: Vitus Bering, sailing for Russia from Kamchatka, reaches Alaska in 1741.
ev.casanova.t: Giacomo Casanova, born in Venice in 1725, takes his degree at Padua and serves in Rome and Corfu. He is in Paris in 1750, escapes the Piombi prison of Venice and is back in Paris in January 1757, visits Voltaire in Switzerland in 1760 and London in 1763, Berlin and Catherine’s St Petersburg in the mid-1760s, and is expelled from Warsaw after a duel in 1766. From 1785 he is librarian at Dux in Bohemia, where he writes his Histoire de ma vie and dies in 1798.
ev.saudi-1744.t: Muhammad ibn Saud founds the first Saudi state in Arabia in 1744. In 1747 Ahmad Shah Durrani founds the Durrani Empire in Afghanistan.
ev.lisbon-1755.t: The earthquake of 1755 kills up to 100,000 people in Lisbon.
ev.dzungar-1755.t: Under the Qianlong Emperor the Qing destroy the Dzungar Khanate; the genocide of 1755 depopulates northern Xinjiang.
ev.seven-years-war.t: The European powers fight worldwide from 1756 to 1763.
ev.plassey-1757.t: The British conquest of Bengal begins with Plassey in 1757.
ev.panipat-1761.t: The Maratha Empire is defeated at Panipat in 1761, the third great battle on the same field.
ev.catherine-1762.t: Catherine the Great’s reign begins in 1762. Her wars with the Ottomans win Russia the Black Sea shore, and Poland is partitioned from 1772.
ev.ayutthaya-1767.t: The Burmese invade Siam in 1765–1767 and destroy Ayutthaya, the capital since 1350.
ev.company-rule.t: After Plassey in 1757 and Buxar in 1764 the East India Company takes the diwani of Bengal and Bihar in 1765; the Regulating Act of 1773 makes Warren Hastings the first Governor-General. At its height the Company accounts for about half of world trade and its three presidency armies number about 260,000 men. Company rule covers about 1,940,000 km² in 1858, when after the rebellion of 1857 the Government of India Act of 2 August hands India to the Crown.
ev.cook-first-voyage.t: The Endeavour leaves Plymouth on 26 August 1768, observes the transit of Venus at Tahiti in June 1769, charts New Zealand, lands at Botany Bay on 29 April 1770 and anchors in the Downs on 12 July 1771.
ev.california-missions-1769.t: Spain founds the first of 21 missions in California in 1769.
ev.bengal-famine-1770.t: Famine kills about a third of the people of Bengal in 1770, five years after the East India Company takes the province’s revenues.
ev.moscow-plague-1771.t: Russian troops at Focșani in Moldavia found the first signs in January 1770, in the war with the Ottomans, brought by prisoners and booty. The plague reached Bryansk by August and was diagnosed in Moscow in December 1770. It peaked in September 1771, when Governor Saltykov fled, the shut city rioted, and Catherine II sent Grigory Orlov with four regiments.
ev.partitions-poland.t: Three partitions between 1772 and 1795 end the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth.
ev.pugachev-1773.t: Yemelyan Pugachev’s rebellion against Catherine begins in 1773, two years after the plague riot in Moscow.
ev.kuchuk-kainarji-1774.t: Signed on 21 July 1774, the treaty ends the Russo-Turkish War of 1768–74. Russia gains Azov, Kerch and Yenikale, Kinburn on the Dnieper estuary, free passage of the Bosporus and Dardanelles and a voice for the Orthodox Christians of the Ottoman lands; the Crimean Khanate is made independent of the sultan.
ev.watt-1776.t: James Watt's improved engine goes to work in 1776.
ev.declaration-1776.t: The Second Continental Congress adopts the Declaration at Philadelphia in 1776.
ev.cook-third-voyage.t: Cook leaves Plymouth on 12 July 1776, sights Hawaii on 18 January 1778, reaches Nootka Sound in March and passes the Bering Strait in August 1778 before the ice turns him back. He is killed at Kealakekua Bay on 14 February 1779; the ships reach the Nore in October 1780.
ev.wealth-of-nations-1776.t: Adam Smith publishes The Wealth of Nations in 1776, the year of the American Declaration of Independence and of Watt’s engine.
ev.herschel-uranus-1781.t: William Herschel announces the planet Uranus in 1781. Jan Ingenhousz had described photosynthesis in 1779.
ev.crimea-1783.t: Catherine’s manifesto of 19 April 1783, pressed by Potemkin, annexes the Crimean Khanate. The Black Sea Fleet is counted founded on 13 May 1783 with its base at Sevastopol; the Ottomans recognise the loss in a treaty signed on 28 December 1783 (8 January 1784).
ev.goethe-italy.t: Goethe slips away from Karlsbad on 3 September 1786 and crosses the Brenner to Verona, Vicenza and Venice. He reaches Rome on 29 October, sits for Tischbein, sees Naples, Vesuvius, Pompeii and Paestum and tours Sicily in 1787, then stays another year in Rome before going home to Weimar in June 1788.
ev.first-fleet-1788.t: The First Fleet arrives in Australia in 1788.
ev.french-revolution.t: The Revolution begins in Paris in 1789.
ev.haiti.t: The slaves of Saint-Domingue rise in 1791; Haiti is independent in 1804.
ev.napoleon-italy.t: Napoleon's first command: Montenotte in April 1796, the bridge at Lodi in May, Arcole in November, Rivoli in January 1797 and peace with Austria at Campo Formio in October.
ev.jenner-1796.t: Edward Jenner gives the first smallpox vaccination in 1796. Smallpox was then killing about 400,000 people a year.
ev.napoleon-egypt.t: The expedition sails in May 1798, wins at the Pyramids on 21 July and takes Cairo, but Nelson destroys the fleet at the Nile on 3 August; Napoleon leaves Egypt for Paris on 23 August 1799.
ev.brumaire-1799.t: Napoleon overthrows the Directory on 9–10 November 1799 and crowns himself emperor on 2 December 1804.
ev.humboldt-1799.t: Alexander von Humboldt and Aimé Bonpland sail from A Coruña on 5 June 1799, land at Cumaná in July and travel up the Orinoco and the Casiquiare in 1800. They cross Cuba and the Andes to Quito, reach about 5,878 m on Chimborazo on 23 June 1802, go on to Lima and Mexico, meet Jefferson in Washington and land at Bordeaux in August 1804.
ev.anaesthesia-1842.t: Hanaoka Seishū in Japan gives the first modern general anaesthetic in 1804. In the West anaesthesia is first used in surgery in 1842, and chloroform follows in 1847.
ev.first-locomotive-1804.t: The first steam locomotive runs in 1804, twenty-one years before the Stockton and Darlington Railway. Morphine is isolated the same year.
ev.fulani-jihad-1804.t: The Fulani jihad is fought in what is now northern Nigeria from 1804 to 1810, while the Barbary Wars bring American warships to North Africa.
ev.trafalgar-1805.t: Nelson destroys the French and Spanish fleets off Cape Trafalgar on 21 October 1805.
ev.austerlitz-1805.t: Napoleon defeats the Russian and Austrian emperors at Austerlitz on 2 December 1805.
ev.jena-1806.t: Prussia is crushed at Jena and Auerstedt on 14 October 1806; the Treaty of Tilsit with Russia follows on 25 June 1807.
ev.musket-wars.t: Māori iwi armed with muskets fight one another across New Zealand from 1807 to 1837. In Tasmania the Black War of 1828–1832 nearly destroys the Aboriginal people.
ev.brazil-court-1808.t: The Portuguese court moves to Rio de Janeiro in 1808. Pedro I declares Brazil independent on 7 September 1822.
ev.peninsular-war.t: For more than six years Wellington’s Anglo-Portuguese army and Spanish guerrillas fight the French in Spain: 60 major battles and 30 sieges, until Vitoria on 21 June 1813 breaks French power there.
ev.wagram-1809.t: Napoleon defeats the Austrians under Archduke Charles at Wagram on 5–6 July 1809; the Treaty of Schönbrunn follows in October.
ev.mexico-independence-1810.t: The Grito de Dolores of 1810 begins the Mexican War of Independence; Mexico is independent in 1821, the year Central America breaks from Spain.
ev.napoleon-russia.t: About 450,000 men of the Grande Armée cross the Niemen on 24 June 1812. Smolensk is fought on 16–18 August and Borodino on 7 September, the bloodiest day of the wars, with at least 70,000 casualties; Napoleon enters an evacuated, burning Moscow on 14 September. The retreat begins in October; at the Berezina in November only about 27,000 fit soldiers remain, and the last invaders leave Russia on 14 December.
ev.leipzig-1813.t: The allies defeat Napoleon at Leipzig on 16–19 October 1813; he abdicates on 4 April 1814 and goes to Elba.
ev.waterloo-1815.t: Napoleon returns to Paris on 20 March 1815 and is beaten at Waterloo on 18 June.
ev.tambora-1815.t: Mount Tambora on Sumbawa erupts in 1815 and kills at least 71,000 people.
ev.european-mass-migration.t: About 60 million Europeans left for the Americas and Australia between 1815 and 1930. The United States took 32,244,000 arrivals between 1821 and 1932, Argentina 6,405,000, Canada 5,206,000 and Brazil 4,431,000; 13 million people left Italy between 1880 and 1915 alone, the largest documented voluntary emigration in history.
ev.shaka-1816.t: Shaka takes power over the Zulu in 1816; by 1828 the Zulu Kingdom is the largest in southern Africa. The British annex it after the war of 1879.
ev.cholera-1817.t: Cholera broke out at Jessore in the Ganges delta in 1817 and reached Calcutta in September. It spread across India and east to Bangkok and Manila in 1820, Java, Oman and China in 1821 and Japan in 1822. Westward it went up the Gulf to Basra and Baghdad and in 1823 reached Astrakhan on the Caspian, Zanzibar and Mauritius.
ev.boyaca-1819.t: Bolívar's victory at Boyacá in 1819 frees Gran Colombia, which breaks up in 1830.
ev.singapore-1819.t: The British East India Company establishes Singapore in 1819.
ev.liberia-1820.t: Liberia is founded in 1820 for freed American slaves.
ev.greek-independence.t: Greece fights free of Ottoman rule between 1821 and 1830.
ev.photograph-1827.t: Nicéphore Niépce makes his first heliographs in 1822 and takes the first photograph in 1827.
ev.stockton-darlington-1825.t: The Stockton and Darlington Railway opens in 1825; the first steam locomotive had run in 1804.
ev.decembrists-1825.t: Officers gather their troops on Senate Square in December 1825 and are dispersed with artillery.
ev.cholera-1826.t: The second pandemic rose in the Ganges delta in 1826, was rampant in Afghanistan and Persia in 1829 and reached Orenburg in the southern Urals on 26 August that year. Russia’s cities had it by 1831, Russian soldiers carried it into Poland, and it reached Sunderland in October 1831 and London and Paris in 1832. A ship brought it to Quebec on 28 April 1832, and it went on to New York, Detroit and Mexico.
ev.algeria-1830.t: France invades Algeria and occupies it in 1830–1831.
ev.lds-1830.t: The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints is established in 1830. In Persia the Báb announces his revelation in 1844.
ev.darwin-beagle.t: HMS Beagle leaves Plymouth on 27 December 1831 with the young Charles Darwin. She surveys Brazil, the Plate, Tierra del Fuego and the Falklands, rounds to Valparaíso, reaches the Galápagos on 15 September 1835 and crosses the Pacific to Tahiti, New Zealand and Sydney; the voyage ends on 2 October 1836, almost five years after it began.
ev.telegraph-1844.t: Telegraphy is patented in 1837; the first publicly funded line runs from Baltimore to Washington in 1844.
ev.opium-war.t: Britain fights the Qing over the opium trade from 1839 to 1842.
ev.irish-famine.t: Potato blight from 1845 to 1852 killed about one million people and sent over one million more abroad during the famine; at least 2.1 million left Ireland between 1845 and 1855. Of the more than 100,000 who sailed to Canada in 1847 about one in five died, over 5,000 of them at Grosse Île. Ireland’s population fell by 20–25% and kept falling for a century.
ev.cholera-1846.t: From India the third pandemic reached Mecca in 1846, killing more than 15,000, and Russia in 1847. It struck England, Ireland and Paris in 1848–49 and ran up the Mississippi in 1849 to New Orleans and St Louis, and to Nashville, where it killed James K. Polk. In London in 1854 John Snow tied the Broad Street outbreak to a water pump, and the handle was removed.
ev.revolutions-1848.t: Risings sweep Europe in 1848, from Paris to Vienna, Berlin, Budapest and Milan.
ev.taiping.t: The Taiping Heavenly Kingdom is proclaimed in 1851, takes Nanjing in 1853 and is destroyed in 1864.
ev.crimean-war.t: Britain, France and the Ottomans fight Russia from 1853 to 1856; Sevastopol is besieged.
ev.perry-1853.t: Commodore Perry’s gunships threaten Edo in 1853–1854 and the policy of sakoku formally ends. Fifteen years later the shogunate falls.
ev.bessemer-1855.t: The Bessemer process of 1855 makes mass-produced steel possible; the world’s first oil refinery opens in Romania in 1856.
ev.third-plague-pandemic.t: Plague broke out in the copper-mining country of Yunnan in 1855, as Han Chinese workers poured in. It killed about 80,000 in Guangzhou in 1894 and reached Hong Kong, where Yersin isolated the bacillus, then Bombay in 1896, Calcutta and Madagascar in 1898, Hawaii, San Francisco, Australia and the Cape by 1900, and Manchuria, as pneumonic plague, in 1910–11. The WHO counted the pandemic active until 1960.
ev.indian-rebellion-1857.t: Sepoys rise at Meerut and Delhi in 1857; the Company's rule ends.
ev.origin-1859.t: Darwin publishes On the Origin of Species in 1859.
ev.italian-unification.t: The Franco-Austrian war of 1859 opens the wars of unification; Rome is Italy's capital after 1870–1871.
ev.serfs-1861.t: Alexander II's manifesto of 1861 frees the serfs of Russia.
ev.us-civil-war.t: The Union and the Confederacy fight from 1861 to 1865.
ev.mendel-1865.t: Maxwell publishes his equations in 1861, Mendel his laws of inheritance in 1865 and Mendeleev the periodic table in 1869.
ev.gettysburg-1863.t: Gettysburg, fought on 1–3 July 1863, is the turning point of the war: more than 50,000 casualties, about 28,000 of them Confederate. Vicksburg falls the same month and the Union holds the Mississippi; the Emancipation Proclamation of 1 January 1863 had declared free more than 3.5 million of the 4 million enslaved.
ev.cholera-1863-1923.n: The fourth, fifth and sixth cholera pandemics
ev.cholera-1863-1923.t: The fourth pandemic left the Ganges delta with pilgrims for Mecca and reached Constantinople in June 1865, then Europe, Zanzibar and, by 1873, the United States, along the ports and rivers. The fifth came out of India in 1881 and struck Baku, Astrakhan and Hamburg in 1892. The sixth, from 1899, hit Egypt, Arabia, Persia, India, Russia and the Philippines and reached Naples in 1910.
ev.kimberley-1867.n: Diamonds and gold in South Africa
ev.kimberley-1867.t: Diamonds are found at Kimberley in 1867 and gold in the Transvaal in 1886.
ev.meiji-1868.t: Power returns to the emperor in 1868 and the court moves from Kyoto to Tokyo; the Boshin War of 1868–1869 ends the shogunate.
ev.german-unification-1871.t: The Franco-Prussian War of 1870–1871 ends in the unification of Germany under Prussia; the empire is proclaimed at Versailles.
ev.sedan-1870.t: Napoleon III surrenders at Sedan on 2 September 1870 and is taken prisoner with about 104,000 soldiers. Paris is besieged from September and capitulates on 28 January 1871; by the Treaty of Frankfurt France cedes Alsace-Lorraine and pays 5 billion francs.
ev.telephone-1876.t: The first telephone call is made in 1876 and the first exchange opens at New Haven in 1878.
ev.electric-light-1879.t: Edison's practical bulb of 1879 is followed by the first large power utilities in 1882.
ev.isandlwana-1879.t: The Anglo-Zulu War of 1879 ends in British victory and the annexation of the Zulu Kingdom. In the Andes Chile fights Peru and Bolivia in the War of the Pacific from 1879 to 1883.
ev.mahdi-1881.t: Muhammad Ahmad proclaims himself the Mahdi in the Sudan in 1881 and declares war on Egypt, which Britain occupies in 1882. The Mahdist state is crushed at Omdurman in 1898.
ev.berlin-conference.n: The Berlin Conference and the scramble for Africa
ev.berlin-conference.t: The Berlin Conference of 1884–1885 sets the rules of partition; by 1898 almost the whole of Africa is colonised.
